title: Manipur Governor and Chief Minister Pay Tribute to Army Captain and Sepoy Killed in Vehicle Accident
summary: Manipur Governor Ajay Kumar Bhalla and Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh paid tribute to Captain Hanuman Ram and Sepoy Mali Jayesh Himmat at Imphal Airport after their deaths in an Army vehicle accident.
body:
IMPHAL: Naga legislators have strongly condemned the November 13 ambush near New Heaven along National Highway 202 in Manipur’s Ukhrul district, which claimed the lives of four civilians, and called for stronger security arrangements, including the replacement of central security forces with state personnel.

The legislators expressed their concerns during a visit to the mortuary at the Jawaharlal Nehru Institute of Medical Sciences (JNIMS) in Imphal, where the bodies of the four victims were brought. The visit was led by MLA Leishiyo Keishing and was attended by Hill Areas Committee Chairman and MLA Dinganglung Gangmei, MLA Kashim Vashum and MLA Tongbram Robindro.

People from different communities, including Naga and Meitei groups, also gathered at the mortuary to express solidarity with the bereaved families. A prayer service was held in memory of the deceased.

**Leishiyo Keishing Calls for Stronger Highway Security**

Condemning the attack, MLA Leishiyo Keishing described the incident as barbaric and unforgivable. He said suspected armed militants had carried out the attack from close range, highlighting the need to strengthen security along vulnerable stretches of national highways.

Keishing said violence against civilians must be condemned by everyone, irrespective of caste or community. While acknowledging the efforts being made by the state government to protect lives and property, he pointed out the challenges of deploying security personnel across the state's extensive forested areas.

Referring to previous ambushes along national highways, the MLA observed that earlier attacks had generally involved firing from a distance, whereas the latest incident involved an attack at close range. He said this change in the nature of the attacks highlighted the need for a stronger and more effective security mechanism.

Keishing also called for the replacement of central security forces deployed in Manipur with state security personnel. He questioned the effectiveness of the existing security arrangements, alleging that several ambushes and attacks had taken place in areas where central forces were stationed.

He further referred to a meeting convened by Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh with civil society organisations on Friday to discuss the prevailing security situation.

**Dinganglung Gangmei Demands Decisive Action**

Hill Areas Committee Chairman and MLA Dinganglung Gangmei also condemned the killing of the four civilians, describing the incident as beyond condemnation.

Gangmei said violence in Manipur had continued for more than four years and called for decisive action against armed groups operating in the state.

"I have asked all law enforcement agencies and decision-makers to take firm decisions to root out militants and anti-state elements creating havoc in our state. We have witnessed the hidden agenda of a proxy war, and we are not happy," Gangmei said.

He urged the authorities to take concrete measures to address the security situation and prevent further attacks.

**Four Civilians Killed in New Heaven Ambush**

The condemnation follows the killing of four civilians in an ambush near New Heaven along NH-202 in Ukhrul district on November 13. The victims were travelling towards Imphal when unidentified armed assailants opened fire on their vehicles.

The deceased were identified as Kapangkhui RS and Haoleila RS from Shangshak Khullen village, and Tychicus Ngalung and Tanmila Keishing from Tashar village.

The attack has prompted strong reactions from Naga organisations and public representatives, with demands for accountability, improved highway security and action against those responsible.

The calls by the Naga MLAs add to the growing pressure on the state and central governments to review security arrangements along vulnerable highway routes and take steps to prevent further civilian casualties.
author: Mirror Lilong Desk
